outline.description: Introduce the motivation behind 1-bit Large Language Models, the costs of scaling conventional FP16/BF16 Transformers, and the vision behind BitNet b1.58 as a high-performance, cost-efficient alternative.
subtopics: The scaling of LLMs and resource constraints
Economic and environmental costs of FP16/BF16 computation
From compression to architectural change: quantization vs 1-bit models
Overview of BitNet and the emergence of BitNet b1.58
What 1.58 bits means: ternary weights and log2(3)

outline.chapter_title: Precision, Quantization, and Compute Cost Fundamentals
outline.description: Build foundational knowledge on numerical precision, quantization, and how precision impacts compute, memory, bandwidth, and energy in LLMs.
subtopics: Floating point vs integer arithmetic in accelerators
Matrix multiplications as the dominant LLM workload
Post-training quantization (PTQ) vs quantization-aware training (QAT)
Activation and weight quantization: ranges, zero-points, and scaling
Memory hierarchy: DRAM, SRAM, bandwidth, and latency trade-offs
Energy models for arithmetic operations and memory access

outline.description: Contrast traditional post-training quantization methods with architectural approaches like BitNet that design for low-bit operation from the start.
subtopics: Limitations of PTQ for very low-bit (<=4-bit) settings
BitNet concept: replacing nn.Linear with BitLinear
Why minimizing multiplications matters
Industry trend toward 4-bit and the leap to 1-bit/ternary

outline.description: Explain the original BitNet idea and how BitNet b1.58 extends it by introducing a ternary weight set {-1, 0, 1} for stronger modeling capacity.
subtopics: BitLinear as a drop-in replacement for Linear layers
Binary/1-bit vs ternary weights: capacity and sparsity
Why include zero? Feature filtering and representational benefits
1.58 bits per weight: storage implications and packing

outline.description: Detail the Transformer backbone and components used in BitNet b1.58, highlighting compatibility with the LLaMA family for easy integration.
subtopics: LLaMA-alike components: RMSNorm, SwiGLU, rotary embeddings
Bias removal rationale
BitLinear blocks in attention and MLP
8-bit activations design choice
Integration with HuggingFace, vLLM, and llama.cpp

outline.description: Dive into the quantization methodology that constrains weights to {-1, 0, +1} and uses 8-bit activations, along with training-time details.
subtopics: Absmean scaling for weights: W_tilde = RoundClip(W/(gamma+epsilon), -1, 1)
Computing gamma as mean absolute weight magnitude
RoundClip: rounding and clipping behavior

Training from scratch vs finetuning considerations

outline.description: Explain how ternary weights enable almost multiplication-free matrix multiplications, the resulting kernel design, and systemic benefits.
subtopics: Replacing FP multiply-adds with integer additions
Bit-packing and accumulation width considerations
GPU kernels: using a 2-bit kernel (Ladder) for BitNet b1.58
Latency, throughput, and memory traffic improvements
Implications for accelerator design and utilization

outline.description: Cover datasets, token budgets, and experimental configurations used to evaluate BitNet b1.58 against FP16 LLaMA baselines.
subtopics: Pretraining on RedPajama for 100B tokens
Model scales evaluated: 3B, 3.9B, 7B, 13B, 70B
StableLM-3B-aligned 2T-token recipe for 3B-scale models

outline.description: Define the metrics and tasks used to assess perplexity and downstream task performance, and how zero-shot evaluation is performed.

lm-evaluation-harness workflow

outline.description: Present and interpret the core performance results showing BitNet b1.58 matching or exceeding FP16 LLaMA baselines starting from ~3B parameters.

3.9B BitNet b1.58 outperforming 3B FP16 LLaMA on tasks

outline.description: Analyze system-level efficiency gains: speed-ups, memory reductions, and throughput scaling with model size and batch size.
subtopics: Inference latency per output token with FasterTransformer
Speed-ups: ~2.71x at 3B, ~2.4x at 3.9B vs 3B FP16, ~4.1x at 70B
Memory savings: ~3.55x at 3B; ~3.32x at 3.9B vs 3B FP16
Throughput on 70B: 11x higher max batch, 8.9x throughput on dual A100 80GB via pipeline parallelism
Scaling trends: why larger models benefit more
Embedding layers as FP and their diminishing memory share

outline.description: Quantify energy savings for arithmetic operations and discuss how BitNet b1.58’s compute pattern maps to modern chips and future designs.

Estimated 71.4x arithmetic energy savings for matmul on 7nm
DRAM-to-SRAM transfer reductions due to lower precision

outline.chapter_title: A New Scaling Law: Performance vs Cost
outline.description: Discuss the emergent scaling law where larger 1.58-bit models can be more efficient than much smaller FP16 models in latency, memory, and energy.
